column1: # Game profile of Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection (Switch, update 1.0.3). Plays on the Mac from the photosensitivity warning through the title screen
# and the Arcade menu into a fight in Street Fighter (1987), at 60 fps; on Android it stops at its first EGL call (see README.md)
# Digital Eclipse's Eclipse engine (EclipseApplication), with the arcade games emulated; every game file is in 18 .mbundle bundles (4.97 GB) under Bundle/
# in the RomFS. It renders with NVIDIA's OpenGL through EGL: main imports nine EGL and 56 GL functions directly (no eglGetProcAddress), which the host's GL
# layer answers on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m; the game asks for OpenGL 2.0), so NVIDIA's GL driver (subsdk0) is never loaded. SDK 3.7.0
# The shaders are four small GLSL ES 1.00 sources (two vertex, two pixel) that the engine puts together at run time, in no game file: the NSP script captures
# them by booting the game on the Mac (gl_capture.tsv) and dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates them offline; the host finds each by hash
# main imports the EGL and GL functions only, so NVIDIA's GL driver (subsdk0, NintendoSDK_OpenGL) stays unloaded
# the bundles are already compressed: deflate leaves 1 MB samples of the RomFS at 98-100 %
# the NPDM declares 256 MB of system resource (virtual address memory), so the guest block is 5 GB with a large alias region
# nninitStartup asks for a 3.14 GB heap (0xc9400000), nearly the whole pool: the heap check on the Mac sized the heap region for it (3.25 GB)
# no NVN shaders: the profile's NVN tables stay empty and the GL library comes from gl_shaders.py (gl_capture.tsv)

column2: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection's shaders, all put together by the engine at run time: captured on the Mac, translated by gl_shaders.py, no NVN tables
